issues.legal_issue: A preventive procedure for restricting premises may create distinct procedural classes without violating the constitutional guarantee of equality when the classification has a reasonable relation to the provision’s purpose.
material_facts: The challenged provision covered both cases in which conduct could also be prosecuted under separate penal provisions and cases involving only the preventive premises measure.
The penal provisions required a regular trial and allowed an appeal, while the premises procedure was preventive, summary, and directed at the use of premises.

The premises measure was intended to reduce the likelihood of brothels or prostitution being conducted near public places, and the elements of the penal offences were not identical to those required for the premises measure.
issues.conclusion: The classification under section 18 was reasonable and did not violate Article 14 of the Constitution.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 permits a classification based on a real and substantial distinction that bears a reasonable relation to the object of the law. Section 18 of the Suppression of Immoral Traffic in Women and Girls Act, 1956, addressed premises through a preventive summary procedure, whereas sections 3 and 7 imposed punishment for offences through regular trials with rights of appeal. The classification therefore had a rational connection to the distinct purposes of those provisions and did not offend the principle in State of West Bengal v. Anwar Ali Sarkar.

rule.if: equality_challenge_to_premises_procedure and (case_involves_premises_measure_with_penal_offence or case_involves_premises_measure_only) and procedure_tracks_distinct_purposes

predicates.equality_challenge_to_premises_procedure: A person challenges an enactment’s premises-related procedure as denying equal protection.
predicates.case_involves_premises_measure_with_pena: The case concerns premises subject to a preventive measure and conduct that may also constitute a separately punishable offence.
predicates.case_involves_premises_measure_only: The case concerns premises subject to a preventive measure without a separately prosecuted offence.
predicates.procedure_tracks_distinct_purposes: The law provides different procedures that correspond to the distinct preventive and punitive purposes of the measures.

issues.definition: When an equality challenge concerns a premises procedure, and the law’s procedural differences correspond to distinct purposes across the relevant classes of cases, the classification is constitutionally valid.

issues.legal_issue: When information before a magistrate discloses a cognizable offence, the magistrate cannot bypass the penal process and proceed only with a preventive premises measure; an investigation must be conducted by an authorized officer or be conducted afresh by one.
material_facts: Police reports placed before the magistrate disclosed offences under section 3 of the Act.
The magistrate proceeded under section 18 without first taking action under the penal provisions.
The proceedings before the magistrate were based on police investigations, and the Act restricted valid investigations of offences under it to designated officers.
issues.conclusion: The proceedings taken under the premises measure were unlawful because the magistrate had not first taken action on the disclosed offences under section 3; the magistrate could proceed afresh in accordance with law, including directing a fresh investigation by an authorized officer if required.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 190(1)(b) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, a magistrate must take cognizance of a cognizable offence brought to the magistrate’s notice. Reading the Act harmoniously, where information discloses an offence under section 3 or section 7, the magistrate must first proceed under the applicable penal provision and may take action under section 18 after those cases are disposed of, if appropriate. Under section 13 of the Act, only a specified officer may validly investigate an offence under the Act; if the investigation was not conducted by such an officer, the magistrate may direct a fresh investigation by a competent officer. The Court relied on Delhi Administration v. Ram Singh concerning the authorized investigation of offences under the Act.

predicates.premises_measure_proceeding: A magistrate initiates a proceeding to restrict or attach premises because of their alleged improper use.
predicates.cognizable_offence_disclosed: Information before the magistrate discloses conduct amounting to a cognizable offence.
predicates.penal_case_not_first_disposed: The related penal case has not been dealt with before the premises measure is pursued.

issues.definition: If a premises-measure proceeding concerns information disclosing a cognizable offence and the related penal case has not first been dealt with, the penal process must precede the premises measure.
